**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Manufacturing Monitoring  

An architect claims that once Service-Oriented Architecture is selected for the Manufacturing Monitoring, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Manufacturing Monitoring Platform must integrate with maintenance/ERP service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Service-Oriented Architecture does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** services expose published interfaces and consumers do not depend on provider internals.

**Concrete Manufacturing Monitoring edge case:** an external Manufacturing Monitoring provider changes message semantics without versioning its contract. Calls still connect but data is interpreted incorrectly, so published syntax alone has not delivered meaningful Interoperability.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q01095 — Service-Oriented Architecture vs Broker (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Manufacturing Monitoring  

A team designing the Manufacturing Monitoring is split between **Service-Oriented Architecture** and **Broker** for the following requirement:
The Manufacturing Monitoring Platform must integrate with maintenance/ERP service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Service-Oriented Architecture for the Manufacturing Monitoring.** The requirement is to integrate the Manufacturing Monitoring with independently managed payment, identity or external-data services, which matches Service-Oriented Architecture's problem: integrate independently managed network services through published contracts. Concretely, the Manufacturing Monitoring is a Service Consumer, external capabilities are Service Providers, published REST/SOAP/message contracts are connectors, and a registry, ESB or orchestrator is added only where discovery, transformation or workflow is required.

**Decisive distinction:** Broker is preferable when the central concern is location-transparent invocation of distributed Servers rather than a service ecosystem of independent providers and consumers. Therefore **Broker** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_4_CCPatterns_Broker.pdf

</details>

In the Government Citizen Portal, apply it to integrate the Government Citizen Portal with independently managed payment, identity or external-data services. The architectural problem is to integrate independently managed network services through published contracts.

**Enhanced quality - Interoperability:** In the Supply Chain Platform, consumers depend on published syntax and semantics rather than provider implementation technology; concretely, integrate the Supply Chain Platform with independently managed payment, identity or external-data services.

**Threatened quality - Performance:** remote calls and middleware add latency and independently managed providers may offer weak performance guarantees. This follows from the actual Service-Oriented Architecture elements/relations: the Supply Chain Platform is a Service Consumer, external capabilities are Service Providers, published REST/SOAP/message contracts are connectors, and a registry, ESB or orchestrator is added only where discovery, transformation or workflow is required.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q01119 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Supply Chain Platform  

An architect claims that once Service-Oriented Architecture is selected for the Supply Chain Platform, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Supply Chain Platform must integrate with supplier/logistics service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Service-Oriented Architecture does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** services expose published interfaces and consumers do not depend on provider internals.

**Concrete Supply Chain Platform edge case:** an external Supply Chain Platform provider changes message semantics without versioning its contract. Calls still connect but data is interpreted incorrectly, so published syntax alone has not delivered meaningful Interoperability.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q01120 — Service-Oriented Architecture vs Broker (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Supply Chain Platform  

A team designing the Supply Chain Platform is split between **Service-Oriented Architecture** and **Broker** for the following requirement:
The Supply Chain Platform must integrate with supplier/logistics service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Service-Oriented Architecture for the Supply Chain Platform.** The requirement is to integrate the Supply Chain Platform with independently managed payment, identity or external-data services, which matches Service-Oriented Architecture's problem: integrate independently managed network services through published contracts. Concretely, the Supply Chain Platform is a Service Consumer, external capabilities are Service Providers, published REST/SOAP/message contracts are connectors, and a registry, ESB or orchestrator is added only where discovery, transformation or workflow is required.

**Decisive distinction:** Broker is preferable when the central concern is location-transparent invocation of distributed Servers rather than a service ecosystem of independent providers and consumers. Therefore **Broker** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_4_CCPatterns_Broker.pdf

</details>

## Q01121 — Publish-Subscribe (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

University Student Portal: The Student Portal must notify an unknown and changing set of interested users/components whenever a seat becomes available in a preferred class, without the event producer knowing every recipient.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Answer: Publish-Subscribe (Component-and-Connector pattern).**

In the University Student Portal, apply it to send University Student Portal status events to all currently interested users and components without naming each recipient. The architectural problem is to distribute events to a changing set of interested runtime consumers.

**Concrete elements and relations:** the University Student Portal status component is the Publisher, interested notification/dashboard components are Subscribers, and an event distributor or publish-subscribe connector handles announce/listen delivery.

**Quality consequence:** Modifiability may improve because Subscribers can be added or removed without changing Publisher correctness. The main trade-off is Performance: event distribution, fan-out and queueing add latency and processing work.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_10_CCPatterns_Publish-Subscribe.pdf

</details>

**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the component that detects or produces the scenario event is the Publisher; interested users, channels, or components are Subscribers; the event distributor/channel is the publish-subscribe connector. The Publisher announces the event without naming every recipient, and the distributor delivers it to the currently registered interested Subscribers.

## Q01124 — Publish-Subscribe (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

An architect claims that once Publish-Subscribe is selected for the University Student Portal, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Student Portal must notify an unknown and changing set of interested users/components whenever a seat becomes available in a preferred class, without the event producer knowing every recipient.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Publish-Subscribe does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** Publishers announce through the connector and do not directly invoke every concrete Subscriber.

**Concrete University Student Portal edge case:** the University Student Portal Publisher directly calls a fixed list of recipients and waits synchronously for each one. A slow recipient delays all delivery and adding a recipient changes the Publisher, so the intended decoupling and latency characteristics are lost.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_10_CCPatterns_Publish-Subscribe.pdf

</details>

A slow recipient delays all delivery and adding a recipient changes the Publisher, so the intended decoupling and latency characteristics are lost.

## Q01151 — Publish-Subscribe (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Answer: Publish-Subscribe (Component-and-Connector pattern).**

In the Digital Banking App, apply it to send Digital Banking App status events to all currently interested users and components without naming each recipient. The architectural problem is to distribute events to a changing set of interested runtime consumers.

## Q01219 — Publish-Subscribe (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Online Learning Platform  

An architect claims that once Publish-Subscribe is selected for the Online Learning Platform, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Learning Platform must notify an unknown and changing set of interested users/components whenever a new lesson is released, without the event producer knowing every recipient.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Publish-Subscribe does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** Publishers announce through the connector and do not directly invoke every concrete Subscriber.

**Concrete Online Learning Platform edge case:** the Online Learning Platform Publisher directly calls a fixed list of recipients and waits synchronously for each one. A slow recipient delays all delivery and adding a recipient changes the Publisher, so the intended decoupling and latency characteristics are lost.

</details>

## Q01281 — Shared-Data (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

University Student Portal: Multiple independent components of the Student Portal need to persistently read and write the same timetable and academic records; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Answer: Shared-Data (Component-and-Connector pattern).**

In the University Student Portal, apply it to let independent University Student Portal services read and update the same authoritative records. The architectural problem is to let independent components communicate indirectly through a common persistent repository.

**Concrete elements and relations:** the University Student Portal database is the Shared-Data Store, application/reporting/processing services are Data Accessors, and read/write transactions are the data-access connectors.

**Quality consequence:** Modifiability may improve because producers and consumers need not call or know one another directly. The main trade-off is Performance: the central Store can bottleneck and all Accessors remain coupled to its schema and consistency rules.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01282 — Shared-Data (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

For the University Student Portal, assume the architect has chosen Shared-Data to address this requirement: Multiple independent components of the Student Portal need to persistently read and write the same timetable and academic records; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the authoritative repository holding the scenario's shared records is the Shared-Data Store; the independent application components that read or write those records are Data Accessors. Accessors communicate indirectly by reading/writing the repository rather than calling one another to exchange the shared state, so consistency and ownership rules must be defined at the store boundary.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01284 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

An architect claims that once Shared-Data is selected for the University Student Portal, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: Multiple independent components of the Student Portal need to persistently read and write the same timetable and academic records; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Shared-Data does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** Accessors exchange shared state through the Store rather than owning separate incompatible copies.

**Concrete University Student Portal edge case:** every University Student Portal Accessor depends on undocumented columns and one database instance. A schema change breaks all Accessors and a store outage stops them together, so indirect communication has created schema coupling and a single failure point.

</details>

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Shared-Data does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** Accessors exchange shared state through the Store rather than owning separate incompatible copies.

**Concrete E-Commerce Marketplace edge case:** every E-Commerce Marketplace Accessor depends on undocumented columns and one database instance. A schema change breaks all Accessors and a store outage stops them together, so indirect communication has created schema coupling and a single failure point.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01310 — Shared-Data vs Client-Server (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** E-Commerce Marketplace  

A team designing the E-Commerce Marketplace is split between **Shared-Data** and **Client-Server** for the following requirement:
Multiple independent components of the Marketplace need to persistently read and write the same orders, products and carts; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Shared-Data for the E-Commerce Marketplace.** The requirement is to let independent E-Commerce Marketplace services read and update the same authoritative records, which matches Shared-Data's problem: let independent components communicate indirectly through a common persistent repository. Concretely, the E-Commerce Marketplace database is the Shared-Data Store, application/reporting/processing services are Data Accessors, and read/write transactions are the data-access connectors.

**Decisive distinction:** Client-Server is preferable when consumers request a service operation and the Server, rather than a repository, owns the behavior. Therefore **Client-Server** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_7_CCPatterns_Client-Server.pdf

</details>

## Q01311 — Shared-Data (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** Digital Banking App  

Digital Banking App: Multiple independent components of the Banking Application need to persistently read and write the same accounts and transaction history; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Answer: Shared-Data (Component-and-Connector pattern).**

In the Digital Banking App, apply it to let independent Digital Banking App services read and update the same authoritative records. The architectural problem is to let independent components communicate indirectly through a common persistent repository.

**Concrete elements and relations:** the Digital Banking App database is the Shared-Data Store, application/reporting/processing services are Data Accessors, and read/write transactions are the data-access connectors.

**Quality consequence:** Modifiability may improve because producers and consumers need not call or know one another directly. The main trade-off is Performance: the central Store can bottleneck and all Accessors remain coupled to its schema and consistency rules.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Shared-Data for the Ride-Hailing Platform.** The requirement is to let independent Ride-Hailing Platform services read and update the same authoritative records, which matches Shared-Data's problem: let independent components communicate indirectly through a common persistent repository. Concretely, the Ride-Hailing Platform database is the Shared-Data Store, application/reporting/processing services are Data Accessors, and read/write transactions are the data-access connectors.

**Decisive distinction:** Client-Server is preferable when consumers request a service operation and the Server, rather than a repository, owns the behavior. Therefore **Client-Server** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_7_CCPatterns_Client-Server.pdf

</details>

## Q01336 — Shared-Data (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** Video Streaming Service  

Video Streaming Service: Multiple independent components of the Streaming Platform need to persistently read and write the same watch history and catalog; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Answer: Shared-Data (Component-and-Connector pattern).**

In the Video Streaming Service, apply it to let independent Video Streaming Service services read and update the same authoritative records. The architectural problem is to let independent components communicate indirectly through a common persistent repository.

**Concrete elements and relations:** the Video Streaming Service database is the Shared-Data Store, application/reporting/processing services are Data Accessors, and read/write transactions are the data-access connectors.

**Quality consequence:** Modifiability may improve because producers and consumers need not call or know one another directly. The main trade-off is Performance: the central Store can bottleneck and all Accessors remain coupled to its schema and consistency rules.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01339 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Video Streaming Service  

An architect claims that once Shared-Data is selected for the Video Streaming Service, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: Multiple independent components of the Streaming Platform need to persistently read and write the same watch history and catalog; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Shared-Data does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** Accessors exchange shared state through the Store rather than owning separate incompatible copies.

**Concrete Video Streaming Service edge case:** every Video Streaming Service Accessor depends on undocumented columns and one database instance. A schema change breaks all Accessors and a store outage stops them together, so indirect communication has created schema coupling and a single failure point.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Answer: Shared-Data (Component-and-Connector pattern).**

In the Logistics Tracking System, apply it to let independent Logistics Tracking System services read and update the same authoritative records. The architectural problem is to let independent components communicate indirectly through a common persistent repository.

**Concrete elements and relations:** the Logistics Tracking System database is the Shared-Data Store, application/reporting/processing services are Data Accessors, and read/write transactions are the data-access connectors.

**Quality consequence:** Modifiability may improve because producers and consumers need not call or know one another directly. The main trade-off is Performance: the central Store can bottleneck and all Accessors remain coupled to its schema and consistency rules.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

## Q01364 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Logistics Tracking System  

An architect claims that once Shared-Data is selected for the Logistics Tracking System, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: Multiple independent components of the Logistics Platform need to persistently read and write the same shipment status and routes; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Shared-Data does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** Accessors exchange shared state through the Store rather than owning separate incompatible copies.

**Concrete Logistics Tracking System edge case:** every Logistics Tracking System Accessor depends on undocumented columns and one database instance. A schema change breaks all Accessors and a store outage stops them together, so indirect communication has created schema coupling and a single failure point.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01365 — Shared-Data vs Client-Server (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Logistics Tracking System  

A team designing the Logistics Tracking System is split between **Shared-Data** and **Client-Server** for the following requirement:
Multiple independent components of the Logistics Platform need to persistently read and write the same shipment status and routes; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Shared-Data for the Logistics Tracking System.** The requirement is to let independent Logistics Tracking System services read and update the same authoritative records, which matches Shared-Data's problem: let independent components communicate indirectly through a common persistent repository. Concretely, the Logistics Tracking System database is the Shared-Data Store, application/reporting/processing services are Data Accessors, and read/write transactions are the data-access connectors.

**Decisive distinction:** Client-Server is preferable when consumers request a service operation and the Server, rather than a repository, owns the behavior. Therefore **Client-Server** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_7_CCPatterns_Client-Server.pdf

## Q01388 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality trade-off  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Warehouse Management System  

In the Warehouse Management System, Shared-Data is used as described: Multiple independent components of the Warehouse Platform need to persistently read and write the same inventory and order status; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and a different quality attribute that may be threatened. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Enhanced quality - Modifiability:** In the Warehouse Management System, producers and consumers need not call or know one another directly; concretely, let independent Warehouse Management System services read and update the same authoritative records.

**Threatened quality - Performance:** the central Store can bottleneck and all Accessors remain coupled to its schema and consistency rules. This follows from the actual Shared-Data elements/relations: the Warehouse Management System database is the Shared-Data Store, application/reporting/processing services are Data Accessors, and read/write transactions are the data-access connectors.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01389 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Warehouse Management System  

An architect claims that once Shared-Data is selected for the Warehouse Management System, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: Multiple independent components of the Warehouse Platform need to persistently read and write the same inventory and order status; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Shared-Data does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** Accessors exchange shared state through the Store rather than owning separate incompatible copies.

**Concrete Warehouse Management System edge case:** every Warehouse Management System Accessor depends on undocumented columns and one database instance. A schema change breaks all Accessors and a store outage stops them together, so indirect communication has created schema coupling and a single failure point.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01390 — Shared-Data vs Client-Server (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Warehouse Management System  

A team designing the Warehouse Management System is split between **Shared-Data** and **Client-Server** for the following requirement:
Multiple independent components of the Warehouse Platform need to persistently read and write the same inventory and order status; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Shared-Data for the Warehouse Management System.** The requirement is to let independent Warehouse Management System services read and update the same authoritative records, which matches Shared-Data's problem: let independent components communicate indirectly through a common persistent repository. Concretely, the Warehouse Management System database is the Shared-Data Store, application/reporting/processing services are Data Accessors, and read/write transactions are the data-access connectors.

**Decisive distinction:** Client-Server is preferable when consumers request a service operation and the Server, rather than a repository, owns the behavior. Therefore **Client-Server** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_7_CCPatterns_Client-Server.pdf

</details>

## Q01414 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning

**Scenario:** Manufacturing Monitoring

**Required constraint:** Accessors exchange shared state through the Store rather than owning separate incompatible copies.

**Concrete Supply Chain Platform edge case:** every Supply Chain Platform Accessor depends on undocumented columns and one database instance. A schema change breaks all Accessors and a store outage stops them together, so indirect communication has created schema coupling and a single failure point.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01440 — Shared-Data vs Client-Server (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Supply Chain Platform  

A team designing the Supply Chain Platform is split between **Shared-Data** and **Client-Server** for the following requirement:
Multiple independent components of the Supply Chain Platform need to persistently read and write the same inventory, suppliers and orders; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Shared-Data for the Supply Chain Platform.** The requirement is to let independent Supply Chain Platform services read and update the same authoritative records, which matches Shared-Data's problem: let independent components communicate indirectly through a common persistent repository. Concretely, the Supply Chain Platform database is the Shared-Data Store, application/reporting/processing services are Data Accessors, and read/write transactions are the data-access connectors.

**Decisive distinction:** Client-Server is preferable when consumers request a service operation and the Server, rather than a repository, owns the behavior. Therefore **Client-Server** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_7_CCPatterns_Client-Server.pdf

</details>

## Q01441 — Map-Reduce (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

University Student Portal: The Student Portal must analyze multi-year learning analytics logs at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Answer: Map-Reduce (Allocation pattern).**

In the University Student Portal, apply it to analyze the University Student Portal historical event/log dataset in parallel. The architectural problem is to process very large batch datasets using infrastructure-managed parallel work.

**Concrete elements and relations:** Map workers process University Student Portal input partitions into key/value records, infrastructure shuffles and sorts equal keys, Reduce workers aggregate each group, and the infrastructure deploys, monitors and reruns tasks.

**Quality consequence:** Performance may improve because parallel Map and Reduce tasks can increase batch throughput. The main trade-off is Performance: startup, shuffle/sort and synchronization overhead or partition skew can erase the parallel benefit.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q01442 — Map-Reduce (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

For the University Student Portal, assume the architect has chosen Map-Reduce to address this requirement: The Student Portal must analyze multi-year learning analytics logs at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the large input/log files are partitioned by the Infrastructure; Map workers transform each partition into intermediate key/value records; shuffle/sort groups equal keys; Reduce workers aggregate each group into the required result. The Infrastructure distributes tasks, moves intermediate data, monitors workers, and reruns failed work.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q01444 — Map-Reduce (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

An architect claims that once Map-Reduce is selected for the University Student Portal, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Student Portal must analyze multi-year learning analytics logs at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Map-Reduce does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** work must be partitionable into Map, shuffle/sort and Reduce stages managed by the infrastructure.

**Concrete University Student Portal edge case:** one University Student Portal partition contains most records for a hot key. One Reduce worker becomes the straggler while others idle, so total completion time is set by that worker and adding workers does not deliver the expected Performance gain.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

A team designing the Flight Booking System is split between **Map-Reduce** and **Pipe-and-Filter** for the following requirement:
The Flight Booking System must analyze historical booking/search logs at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Map-Reduce for the Flight Booking System.** The requirement is to analyze the Flight Booking System historical event/log dataset in parallel, which matches Map-Reduce's problem: process very large batch datasets using infrastructure-managed parallel work. Concretely, Map workers process Flight Booking System input partitions into key/value records, infrastructure shuffles and sorts equal keys, Reduce workers aggregate each group, and the infrastructure deploys, monitors and reruns tasks.

**Decisive distinction:** Pipe-and-Filter is preferable for successive stream transformations where each item moves through ordered Filters. Therefore **Pipe-and-Filter** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

</details>

## Q01469 — Map-Reduce (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** E-Commerce Marketplace  

An architect claims that once Map-Reduce is selected for the E-Commerce Marketplace, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Marketplace must analyze clickstream and order history at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Map-Reduce does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** work must be partitionable into Map, shuffle/sort and Reduce stages managed by the infrastructure.

**Concrete E-Commerce Marketplace edge case:** one E-Commerce Marketplace partition contains most records for a hot key. One Reduce worker becomes the straggler while others idle, so total completion time is set by that worker and adding workers does not deliver the expected Performance gain.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Map-Reduce for the Smart Traffic Platform.** The requirement is to analyze the Smart Traffic Platform historical event/log dataset in parallel, which matches Map-Reduce's problem: process very large batch datasets using infrastructure-managed parallel work. Concretely, Map workers process Smart Traffic Platform input partitions into key/value records, infrastructure shuffles and sorts equal keys, Reduce workers aggregate each group, and the infrastructure deploys, monitors and reruns tasks.

**Decisive distinction:** Pipe-and-Filter is preferable for successive stream transformations where each item moves through ordered Filters. Therefore **Pipe-and-Filter** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

</details>

## Q01491 — Map-Reduce (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** Ride-Hailing Platform  

Ride-Hailing Platform: The Ride-Hailing Platform must analyze regional trip history at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Answer: Map-Reduce (Allocation pattern).**

In the Ride-Hailing Platform, apply it to analyze the Ride-Hailing Platform historical event/log dataset in parallel. The architectural problem is to process very large batch datasets using infrastructure-managed parallel work.

**Concrete elements and relations:** Map workers process Ride-Hailing Platform input partitions into key/value records, infrastructure shuffles and sorts equal keys, Reduce workers aggregate each group, and the infrastructure deploys, monitors and reruns tasks.

**Quality consequence:** Performance may improve because parallel Map and Reduce tasks can increase batch throughput. The main trade-off is Performance: startup, shuffle/sort and synchronization overhead or partition skew can erase the parallel benefit.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

## Q01494 — Map-Reduce (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Ride-Hailing Platform  

An architect claims that once Map-Reduce is selected for the Ride-Hailing Platform, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Ride-Hailing Platform must analyze regional trip history at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Map-Reduce does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** work must be partitionable into Map, shuffle/sort and Reduce stages managed by the infrastructure.

**Concrete Ride-Hailing Platform edge case:** one Ride-Hailing Platform partition contains most records for a hot key. One Reduce worker becomes the straggler while others idle, so total completion time is set by that worker and adding workers does not deliver the expected Performance gain.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q01516 — Map-Reduce (Hard, 6 marks)

**Scenario:** Smart Home Platform  

Smart Home Platform: The Smart Home Platform must analyze long-term household sensor history at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Answer: Map-Reduce (Allocation pattern).**

In the Smart Home Platform, apply it to analyze the Smart Home Platform historical event/log dataset in parallel. The architectural problem is to process very large batch datasets using infrastructure-managed parallel work.

**Concrete elements and relations:** Map workers process Smart Home Platform input partitions into key/value records, infrastructure shuffles and sorts equal keys, Reduce workers aggregate each group, and the infrastructure deploys, monitors and reruns tasks.

**Quality consequence:** Performance may improve because parallel Map and Reduce tasks can increase batch throughput. The main trade-off is Performance: startup, shuffle/sort and synchronization overhead or partition skew can erase the parallel benefit.

## Q01519 — Map-Reduce (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Smart Home Platform  

An architect claims that once Map-Reduce is selected for the Smart Home Platform, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Smart Home Platform must analyze long-term household sensor history at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Map-Reduce does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** work must be partitionable into Map, shuffle/sort and Reduce stages managed by the infrastructure.

**Concrete Smart Home Platform edge case:** one Smart Home Platform partition contains most records for a hot key. One Reduce worker becomes the straggler while others idle, so total completion time is set by that worker and adding workers does not deliver the expected Performance gain.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q01541 — Map-Reduce (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform  

Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform: The Security Monitoring Platform must analyze enterprise security logs at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Answer: Map-Reduce (Allocation pattern).**

In the Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform, apply it to analyze the Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform historical event/log dataset in parallel. The architectural problem is to process very large batch datasets using infrastructure-managed parallel work.

**Concrete elements and relations:** Map workers process Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform input partitions into key/value records, infrastructure shuffles and sorts equal keys, Reduce workers aggregate each group, and the infrastructure deploys, monitors and reruns tasks.

**Quality consequence:** Performance may improve because parallel Map and Reduce tasks can increase batch throughput. The main trade-off is Performance: startup, shuffle/sort and synchronization overhead or partition skew can erase the parallel benefit.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

## Q01544 — Map-Reduce (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform  

An architect claims that once Map-Reduce is selected for the Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Security Monitoring Platform must analyze enterprise security logs at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Map-Reduce does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** work must be partitionable into Map, shuffle/sort and Reduce stages managed by the infrastructure.

**Concrete Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform edge case:** one Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform partition contains most records for a hot key. One Reduce worker becomes the straggler while others idle, so total completion time is set by that worker and adding workers does not deliver the expected Performance gain.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** Medical Imaging Platform  

Medical Imaging Platform: The Imaging Platform must analyze large imaging archive at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Answer: Map-Reduce (Allocation pattern).**

In the Medical Imaging Platform, apply it to analyze the Medical Imaging Platform historical event/log dataset in parallel. The architectural problem is to process very large batch datasets using infrastructure-managed parallel work.

**Concrete elements and relations:** Map workers process Medical Imaging Platform input partitions into key/value records, infrastructure shuffles and sorts equal keys, Reduce workers aggregate each group, and the infrastructure deploys, monitors and reruns tasks.

**Quality consequence:** Performance may improve because parallel Map and Reduce tasks can increase batch throughput. The main trade-off is Performance: startup, shuffle/sort and synchronization overhead or partition skew can erase the parallel benefit.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q01569 — Map-Reduce (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Medical Imaging Platform  

An architect claims that once Map-Reduce is selected for the Medical Imaging Platform, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Imaging Platform must analyze large imaging archive at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Map-Reduce does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** work must be partitionable into Map, shuffle/sort and Reduce stages managed by the infrastructure.

**Concrete Medical Imaging Platform edge case:** one Medical Imaging Platform partition contains most records for a hot key. One Reduce worker becomes the straggler while others idle, so total completion time is set by that worker and adding workers does not deliver the expected Performance gain.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q01570 — Map-Reduce vs Pipe-and-Filter (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Medical Imaging Platform  

A team designing the Medical Imaging Platform is split between **Map-Reduce** and **Pipe-and-Filter** for the following requirement:
The Imaging Platform must analyze large imaging archive at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Map-Reduce for the Medical Imaging Platform.** The requirement is to analyze the Medical Imaging Platform historical event/log dataset in parallel, which matches Map-Reduce's problem: process very large batch datasets using infrastructure-managed parallel work. Concretely, Map workers process Medical Imaging Platform input partitions into key/value records, infrastructure shuffles and sorts equal keys, Reduce workers aggregate each group, and the infrastructure deploys, monitors and reruns tasks.

**Decisive distinction:** Pipe-and-Filter is preferable for successive stream transformations where each item moves through ordered Filters. Therefore **Pipe-and-Filter** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

</details>

**Concrete elements and relations:** Map workers process Online Auction Platform input partitions into key/value records, infrastructure shuffles and sorts equal keys, Reduce workers aggregate each group, and the infrastructure deploys, monitors and reruns tasks.

**Quality consequence:** Performance may improve because parallel Map and Reduce tasks can increase batch throughput. The main trade-off is Performance: startup, shuffle/sort and synchronization overhead or partition skew can erase the parallel benefit.

## Q01594 — Map-Reduce (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Online Auction Platform  

An architect claims that once Map-Reduce is selected for the Online Auction Platform, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Auction Platform must analyze auction/bid history at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Map-Reduce does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** work must be partitionable into Map, shuffle/sort and Reduce stages managed by the infrastructure.

**Concrete Online Auction Platform edge case:** one Online Auction Platform partition contains most records for a hot key. One Reduce worker becomes the straggler while others idle, so total completion time is set by that worker and adding workers does not deliver the expected Performance gain.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q01595 — Map-Reduce vs Pipe-and-Filter (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Online Auction Platform  

A team designing the Online Auction Platform is split between **Map-Reduce** and **Pipe-and-Filter** for the following requirement:
The Auction Platform must analyze auction/bid history at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Map-Reduce for the Online Auction Platform.** The requirement is to analyze the Online Auction Platform historical event/log dataset in parallel, which matches Map-Reduce's problem: process very large batch datasets using infrastructure-managed parallel work. Concretely, Map workers process Online Auction Platform input partitions into key/value records, infrastructure shuffles and sorts equal keys, Reduce workers aggregate each group, and the infrastructure deploys, monitors and reruns tasks.

**Decisive distinction:** Pipe-and-Filter is preferable for successive stream transformations where each item moves through ordered Filters. Therefore **Pipe-and-Filter** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

## Q01601 — Multi-Tier (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

University Student Portal: The Student Portal must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Answer: Multi-Tier (Allocation pattern).**

In the University Student Portal, apply it to deploy the University Student Portal presentation, application processing and data management on separate runtime tiers. The architectural problem is to separate runtime component groups into independently deployed tiers.

**Concrete elements and relations:** browser/mobile components form the presentation tier, University Student Portal services form the application tier, and database components form the data tier; network request/reply connectors cross only permitted tier boundaries.

**Quality consequence:** Security may improve because separate deployment boundaries allow different exposure, privileges and protection policies. The main trade-off is Performance: cross-tier network calls, serialization and chatty interactions add latency.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01602 — Multi-Tier (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

For the University Student Portal, assume the architect has chosen Multi-Tier to address this requirement: The Student Portal must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: user-interface runtime components form the presentation tier, application/business processing forms the application tier, and persistent records/services form the data tier. Request/reply communication crosses the permitted tier boundaries, and each tier is allocated to its own deployable runtime/platform so it can be secured or scaled independently; each component belongs to one tier.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01617 — Multi-Tier (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Digital Game Store  

For the Digital Game Store, assume the architect has chosen Multi-Tier to address this requirement: The Game Distribution Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: user-interface runtime components form the presentation tier, application/business processing forms the application tier, and persistent records/services form the data tier. Request/reply communication crosses the permitted tier boundaries, and each tier is allocated to its own deployable runtime/platform so it can be secured or scaled independently; each component belongs to one tier.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01618 — Multi-Tier (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality benefit and weakness  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Digital Game Store  

In the Digital Game Store, Multi-Tier is used as described: The Game Distribution Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and one source-grounded weakness of the pattern. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality or weakness.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Enhanced quality - Security:** In the Digital Game Store, separate deployment boundaries allow different exposure, privileges and protection policies; concretely, deploy the Digital Game Store presentation, application processing and data management on separate runtime tiers.

**Weakness - Performance:** cross-tier network calls, serialization and chatty interactions add latency. This follows from the actual Multi-Tier elements/relations: browser/mobile components form the presentation tier, Digital Game Store services form the application tier, and database components form the data tier; network request/reply connectors cross only permitted tier boundaries.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01619 — Multi-Tier (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Digital Game Store  

An architect claims that once Multi-Tier is selected for the Digital Game Store, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Game Distribution Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Multi-Tier does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** each runtime component belongs to one tier and communication follows the documented tier rules.

**Concrete Digital Game Store edge case:** all Digital Game Store tiers are placed on one host with the database publicly reachable. The diagram still has three named tiers, but there is no real failure or security isolation, so the expected Security and Availability consequences are not achieved.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01620 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Digital Game Store  

A team designing the Digital Game Store is split between **Multi-Tier** and **Layer** for the following requirement:
The Game Distribution Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Multi-Tier for the Digital Game Store.** The requirement is to deploy the Digital Game Store presentation, application processing and data management on separate runtime tiers, which matches Multi-Tier's problem: separate runtime component groups into independently deployed tiers. Concretely, browser/mobile components form the presentation tier, Digital Game Store services form the application tier, and database components form the data tier; network request/reply connectors cross only permitted tier boundaries.

**Decisive distinction:** Layer is preferable when the concern is logical module responsibilities and allowed source-code dependencies rather than runtime allocation. Therefore **Layer** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

</details>

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: user-interface runtime components form the presentation tier, application/business processing forms the application tier, and persistent records/services form the data tier. ## Q01643 — Multi-Tier (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality benefit and weakness  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Hospital Information System  

In the Hospital Information System, Multi-Tier is used as described: The Hospital Information System must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and one source-grounded weakness of the pattern. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality or weakness.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Enhanced quality - Security:** In the Hospital Information System, separate deployment boundaries allow different exposure, privileges and protection policies; concretely, deploy the Hospital Information System presentation, application processing and data management on separate runtime tiers.

**Weakness - Performance:** cross-tier network calls, serialization and chatty interactions add latency. This follows from the actual Multi-Tier elements/relations: browser/mobile components form the presentation tier, Hospital Information System services form the application tier, and database components form the data tier; network request/reply connectors cross only permitted tier boundaries.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01644 — Multi-Tier (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Hospital Information System  

An architect claims that once Multi-Tier is selected for the Hospital Information System, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Hospital Information System must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Multi-Tier does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** each runtime component belongs to one tier and communication follows the documented tier rules.

**Concrete Hospital Information System edge case:** all Hospital Information System tiers are placed on one host with the database publicly reachable. The diagram still has three named tiers, but there is no real failure or security isolation, so the expected Security and Availability consequences are not achieved.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01645 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Hospital Information System  

A team designing the Hospital Information System is split between **Multi-Tier** and **Layer** for the following requirement:
The Hospital Information System must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Multi-Tier for the Hospital Information System.** The requirement is to deploy the Hospital Information System presentation, application processing and data management on separate runtime tiers, which matches Multi-Tier's problem: separate runtime component groups into independently deployed tiers. Concretely, browser/mobile components form the presentation tier, Hospital Information System services form the application tier, and database components form the data tier; network request/reply connectors cross only permitted tier boundaries.

**Decisive distinction:** Layer is preferable when the concern is logical module responsibilities and allowed source-code dependencies rather than runtime allocation. Therefore **Layer** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.

Request/reply communication crosses the permitted tier boundaries, and each tier is allocated to its own deployable runtime/platform so it can be secured or scaled independently; each component belongs to one tier.
