## Q01668 — Multi-Tier (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality benefit and weakness  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Cloud File Storage  

In the Cloud File Storage, Multi-Tier is used as described: The Cloud Storage Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and one source-grounded weakness of the pattern. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality or weakness.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Enhanced quality - Security:** In the Cloud File Storage, separate deployment boundaries allow different exposure, privileges and protection policies; concretely, deploy the Cloud File Storage presentation, application processing and data management on separate runtime tiers.

**Weakness - Performance:** cross-tier network calls, serialization and chatty interactions add latency. This follows from the actual Multi-Tier elements/relations: browser/mobile components form the presentation tier, Cloud File Storage services form the application tier, and database components form the data tier; network request/reply connectors cross only permitted tier boundaries.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01669 — Multi-Tier (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Cloud File Storage  

An architect claims that once Multi-Tier is selected for the Cloud File Storage, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Cloud Storage Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Reject the guarantee.** Selecting Multi-Tier does not guarantee a quality attribute; the mechanism and constraints must actually hold.

**Required constraint:** each runtime component belongs to one tier and communication follows the documented tier rules.

**Concrete Cloud File Storage edge case:** all Cloud File Storage tiers are placed on one host with the database publicly reachable. The diagram still has three named tiers, but there is no real failure or security isolation, so the expected Security and Availability consequences are not achieved.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01670 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Cloud File Storage  

A team designing the Cloud File Storage is split between **Multi-Tier** and **Layer** for the following requirement:
The Cloud Storage Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Multi-Tier for the Cloud File Storage.** The requirement is to deploy the Cloud File Storage presentation, application processing and data management on separate runtime tiers, which matches Multi-Tier's problem: separate runtime component groups into independently deployed tiers. Concretely, browser/mobile components form the presentation tier, Cloud File Storage services form the application tier, and database components form the data tier; network request/reply connectors cross only permitted tier boundaries.

**Decisive distinction:** Layer is preferable when the concern is logical module responsibilities and allowed source-code dependencies rather than runtime allocation. Therefore **Layer** becomes preferable only when that alternative concern replaces the requirement stated in this question.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

</details>

## Q01694 — Multi-Tier (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Hotel Booking Platform  

An architect claims that once Multi-Tier is selected for the Hotel Booking Platform, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Hotel Booking Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

## Q03673 — Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Bridging and upward calls  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

In the University Student Portal, a strict Layer design is A→B→C. The team proposes (i) A directly uses C for performance and (ii) C emits a one-way callback/event upward to A without depending on a returned answer. Analyze both proposals using the lecture's finer points.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

A→C is **bridging**: it may be permitted, but must be explicitly documented; it can reduce traversal overhead while weakening dependency restriction/modifiability. An **upward call** is not automatically an upward *use*: the lecture defines 'uses' in terms of depending on the answer. A one-way upward notification can be allowed if it does not create a dependency on a response. Be explicit about the relation semantics. Applied to the **University Student Portal**, this means the named University Student Portal elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

</details>

## Q03674 — Publish-Subscribe (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Variant selection  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

The University Student Portal must distribute events related to 'a seat becomes available in a preferred class'. Compare **list-based, broadcast-based and content-based** Publish-Subscribe. Choose a variant for a case with many subscribers but highly selective event predicates and justify the trade-off.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose content-based Publish-Subscribe for the University Student Portal.** List-based delivery is runtime-efficient but maintains explicit subscription lists; broadcast-based is simple and decoupled but makes every subscriber inspect irrelevant events. Content-based matching evaluates event attributes against subscriber predicates, so it fits many subscribers with highly selective interests. The trade-off is extra matching/indexing complexity and latency, which should be measured against the event-delivery response target.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_10_CCPatterns_Publish-Subscribe.pdf

</details>

## Q03675 — Peer-to-Peer (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Discovery, hops and supernodes  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

In a P2P feature for the University Student Portal, peers cannot broadcast discovery indefinitely. Explain the role of search propagation, **hop limits**, and **supernodes**, and show one quality trade-off caused by tightening the hop limit.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Search may propagate peer-to-peer for a bounded number of hops; hop limits control network overhead. Specialized peers/supernodes may index or route searches so ordinary peers reach more resources efficiently. A tighter hop limit can improve performance/network overhead/predictability but reduce discoverability/availability of rare resources. A supernode can improve discovery but may concentrate responsibility and require availability/security hardening. Applied to the **University Student Portal**, this means the named University Student Portal elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q03676 — Pipe-and-Filter (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Pipeline parallelism  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

Three items T1, T2 and T3 are processed in the University Student Portal by Filter A→Filter B→Filter C. Give a valid simultaneous execution snapshot, explain how buffering enables it, then identify why this improves **throughput** without necessarily reducing the end-to-end **latency** of one item.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Example snapshot: A processes T3, B processes T2, C processes T1. Pipes/buffers decouple stage timing until buffers fill, allowing concurrent stage execution. This can increase aggregate throughput because several items are in flight, but T1 still must traverse all mandatory stages, so its own end-to-end latency may remain the sum of stage/queue delays. Applied to the **University Student Portal**, this means the named University Student Portal elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

</details>

## Q03677 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Brutal, 7 marks)

**Type:** ESB, registry, orchestration  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

The University Student Portal uses SOA. Distinguish the roles of a **service registry**, **ESB**, and **orchestration server**. For each, give one benefit and one new risk/overhead. Explain why none of the three is automatically required in every SOA instance.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Registry: providers register and consumers discover services, hiding provider location/identity and improving modifiability; adds discovery dependency/complexity. ESB: routes/transforms protocols/content and can perform security checks, improving interoperability/modifiability; adds latency and failure point. Orchestration server: coordinates multi-service business workflows; adds centralized coordination complexity/failure risk. They are optional architectural elements chosen according to the specific SOA problem. Applied to the **University Student Portal**, this means the named University Student Portal elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q03678 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Replication and coupling  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

The University Student Portal uses Shared-Data. The architect replicates the data store across two regions to reduce outage risk. Explain what quality may improve, then identify two new issues introduced by replication and one coupling problem that remains even if producers/consumers do not know each other.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Replication can improve availability and possibly read performance. New issues include consistency/synchronization, conflict resolution, replication latency, failover routing and operational complexity. Producer/consumer identity coupling is reduced, but accessors can still be coupled through knowledge of the shared **data schema/structure**. Applied to the **University Student Portal**, this means the named University Student Portal elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q03679 — Model-View-Controller (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Many views and constraints  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

The University Student Portal displays the same model through a table, chart and mobile visualization. Explain how MVC keeps them synchronized, why many views/controllers can share one model, and why the lecture constraint that the model should not directly interact with the controller matters.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Model holds application data/state and notifies views of changes; views render/query model; controllers translate user gestures into model/view actions. Multiple views/controllers can share one model because presentation/input concerns are separated. Preventing direct model→controller dependency helps preserve separation and reduces coupling; notifications from model go to interested views rather than making model dependent on specific input-control logic. Applied to the **University Student Portal**, this means the named University Student Portal elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_5_CCPatterns_Model-view Controller.pdf

</details>

## Q03680 — Map-Reduce (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Partition imbalance  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

The University Student Portal uses Map-Reduce on multi-year learning analytics logs. One partition contains 70% of the data while the others are tiny. Explain why adding more processors may fail to improve completion time and connect the answer to the pattern's constraints and overhead.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Map-Reduce benefits depend on dividing the data into similar-sized subsets. A dominant partition becomes a straggler/bottleneck, leaving other processors idle and eroding parallel speedup. Infrastructure still incurs deployment/shuffle/sort/monitoring overhead. Stateless maps/key-value communication do not solve skew automatically; data partitioning must support balanced work. Applied to the **University Student Portal**, this means the named University Student Portal elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q03681 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Distinction  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q4  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

A diagram for the University Student Portal labels 'Presentation', 'Business' and 'Data'. A student concludes it is definitely a Layer pattern. Explain why the labels alone are insufficient and show how the **same names** could describe either Layer or Multi-Tier depending on element/relation semantics.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Layer is a **module pattern**: implementation units grouped into layers with allowed-to-use dependency rules. Multi-Tier is an **allocation/runtime pattern**: runtime components grouped into tiers with communication/allocation constraints. Box labels do not determine semantics. Ask whether the elements are modules and dependencies, or runtime components/tier groupings mapped to platforms. Applied to the **University Student Portal**, this means the named University Student Portal elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

</details>

## Q03683 — Publish-Subscribe (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Variant selection  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Online Trading Platform  

The Online Trading Platform must distribute events related to 'a watched stock reaches a target price'. Compare **list-based, broadcast-based and content-based** Publish-Subscribe. Choose a variant for a case with many subscribers but highly selective event predicates and justify the trade-off.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose content-based Publish-Subscribe for the Online Trading Platform.** List-based delivery is runtime-efficient but maintains explicit subscription lists; broadcast-based is simple and decoupled but makes every subscriber inspect irrelevant events. Content-based matching evaluates event attributes against subscriber predicates, so it fits many subscribers with highly selective interests. The trade-off is extra matching/indexing complexity and latency, which should be measured against the event-delivery response target.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_10_CCPatterns_Publish-Subscribe.pdf

</details>

## Q03684 — Peer-to-Peer (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Discovery, hops and supernodes  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Online Trading Platform  

In a P2P feature for the Online Trading Platform, peers cannot broadcast discovery indefinitely. Explain the role of search propagation, **hop limits**, and **supernodes**, and show one quality trade-off caused by tightening the hop limit.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Search may propagate peer-to-peer for a bounded number of hops; hop limits control network overhead. Specialized peers/supernodes may index or route searches so ordinary peers reach more resources efficiently. A tighter hop limit can improve performance/network overhead/predictability but reduce discoverability/availability of rare resources. A supernode can improve discovery but may concentrate responsibility and require availability/security hardening. Applied to the **Online Trading Platform**, this means the named Online Trading Platform elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q03685 — Pipe-and-Filter (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Pipeline parallelism  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Online Trading Platform  

Three items T1, T2 and T3 are processed in the Online Trading Platform by Filter A→Filter B→Filter C. Give a valid simultaneous execution snapshot, explain how buffering enables it, then identify why this improves **throughput** without necessarily reducing the end-to-end **latency** of one item.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Example snapshot: A processes T3, B processes T2, C processes T1. Pipes/buffers decouple stage timing until buffers fill, allowing concurrent stage execution. This can increase aggregate throughput because several items are in flight, but T1 still must traverse all mandatory stages, so its own end-to-end latency may remain the sum of stage/queue delays. Applied to the **Online Trading Platform**, this means the named Online Trading Platform elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

</details>

## Q03686 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Brutal, 7 marks)

**Type:** ESB, registry, orchestration  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Online Trading Platform  

The Online Trading Platform uses SOA. Distinguish the roles of a **service registry**, **ESB**, and **orchestration server**. For each, give one benefit and one new risk/overhead. Explain why none of the three is automatically required in every SOA instance.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Registry: providers register and consumers discover services, hiding provider location/identity and improving modifiability; adds discovery dependency/complexity. ESB: routes/transforms protocols/content and can perform security checks, improving interoperability/modifiability; adds latency and failure point. Orchestration server: coordinates multi-service business workflows; adds centralized coordination complexity/failure risk. They are optional architectural elements chosen according to the specific SOA problem. Applied to the **Online Trading Platform**, this means the named Online Trading Platform elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q03687 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Replication and coupling  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Online Trading Platform  

The Online Trading Platform uses Shared-Data. The architect replicates the data store across two regions to reduce outage risk. Explain what quality may improve, then identify two new issues introduced by replication and one coupling problem that remains even if producers/consumers do not know each other.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Replication can improve availability and possibly read performance. New issues include consistency/synchronization, conflict resolution, replication latency, failover routing and operational complexity. Producer/consumer identity coupling is reduced, but accessors can still be coupled through knowledge of the shared **data schema/structure**. Applied to the **Online Trading Platform**, this means the named Online Trading Platform elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q03688 — Model-View-Controller (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Many views and constraints  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Online Trading Platform  

The Online Trading Platform displays the same model through a table, chart and mobile visualization. Explain how MVC keeps them synchronized, why many views/controllers can share one model, and why the lecture constraint that the model should not directly interact with the controller matters.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Model holds application data/state and notifies views of changes; views render/query model; controllers translate user gestures into model/view actions. Multiple views/controllers can share one model because presentation/input concerns are separated. Preventing direct model→controller dependency helps preserve separation and reduces coupling; notifications from model go to interested views rather than making model dependent on specific input-control logic. Applied to the **Online Trading Platform**, this means the named Online Trading Platform elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_5_CCPatterns_Model-view Controller.pdf

</details>

## Q03689 — Map-Reduce (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Partition imbalance  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Online Trading Platform  

The Online Trading Platform uses Map-Reduce on historical market ticks. One partition contains 70% of the data while the others are tiny. Explain why adding more processors may fail to improve completion time and connect the answer to the pattern's constraints and overhead.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Map-Reduce benefits depend on dividing the data into similar-sized subsets. A dominant partition becomes a straggler/bottleneck, leaving other processors idle and eroding parallel speedup. Infrastructure still incurs deployment/shuffle/sort/monitoring overhead. Stateless maps/key-value communication do not solve skew automatically; data partitioning must support balanced work. Applied to the **Online Trading Platform**, this means the named Online Trading Platform elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q03690 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Distinction  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q4  
**Scenario:** Online Trading Platform  

A diagram for the Online Trading Platform labels 'Presentation', 'Business' and 'Data'. A student concludes it is definitely a Layer pattern. Explain why the labels alone are insufficient and show how the **same names** could describe either Layer or Multi-Tier depending on element/relation semantics.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Layer is a **module pattern**: implementation units grouped into layers with allowed-to-use dependency rules. Multi-Tier is an **allocation/runtime pattern**: runtime components grouped into tiers with communication/allocation constraints. Box labels do not determine semantics. Ask whether the elements are modules and dependencies, or runtime components/tier groupings mapped to platforms. Applied to the **Online Trading Platform**, this means the named Online Trading Platform elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q03691 — Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Bridging and upward calls  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Electricity Utility App  

In the Electricity Utility App, a strict Layer design is A→B→C. The team proposes (i) A directly uses C for performance and (ii) C emits a one-way callback/event upward to A without depending on a returned answer. Analyze both proposals using the lecture's finer points.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

A→C is **bridging**: it may be permitted, but must be explicitly documented; it can reduce traversal overhead while weakening dependency restriction/modifiability. An **upward call** is not automatically an upward *use*: the lecture defines 'uses' in terms of depending on the answer. A one-way upward notification can be allowed if it does not create a dependency on a response. Be explicit about the relation semantics. Applied to the **Electricity Utility App**, this means the named Electricity Utility App elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

</details>

This can increase aggregate throughput because several items are in flight, but T1 still must traverse all mandatory stages, so its own end-to-end latency may remain the sum of stage/queue delays. Applied to the **Flight Booking System**, this means the named Flight Booking System elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

</details>

## Q03713 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Brutal, 7 marks)

**Type:** ESB, registry, orchestration  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Flight Booking System  

The Flight Booking System uses SOA. Distinguish the roles of a **service registry**, **ESB**, and **orchestration server**. For each, give one benefit and one new risk/overhead. Explain why none of the three is automatically required in every SOA instance.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Registry: providers register and consumers discover services, hiding provider location/identity and improving modifiability; adds discovery dependency/complexity. ESB: routes/transforms protocols/content and can perform security checks, improving interoperability/modifiability; adds latency and failure point. Orchestration server: coordinates multi-service business workflows; adds centralized coordination complexity/failure risk. They are optional architectural elements chosen according to the specific SOA problem. Applied to the **Flight Booking System**, this means the named Flight Booking System elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q03714 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Replication and coupling  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Flight Booking System  

The Flight Booking System uses Shared-Data. The architect replicates the data store across two regions to reduce outage risk. Explain what quality may improve, then identify two new issues introduced by replication and one coupling problem that remains even if producers/consumers do not know each other.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Replication can improve availability and possibly read performance. New issues include consistency/synchronization, conflict resolution, replication latency, failover routing and operational complexity. Producer/consumer identity coupling is reduced, but accessors can still be coupled through knowledge of the shared **data schema/structure**. Applied to the **Flight Booking System**, this means the named Flight Booking System elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q03715 — Model-View-Controller (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Many views and constraints  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Flight Booking System  

The Flight Booking System displays the same model through a table, chart and mobile visualization. Explain how MVC keeps them synchronized, why many views/controllers can share one model, and why the lecture constraint that the model should not directly interact with the controller matters.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Model holds application data/state and notifies views of changes; views render/query model; controllers translate user gestures into model/view actions. Multiple views/controllers can share one model because presentation/input concerns are separated. Preventing direct model→controller dependency helps preserve separation and reduces coupling; notifications from model go to interested views rather than making model dependent on specific input-control logic. Applied to the **Flight Booking System**, this means the named Flight Booking System elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_5_CCPatterns_Model-view Controller.pdf

</details>

## Q03716 — Map-Reduce (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Partition imbalance  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Flight Booking System  

The Flight Booking System uses Map-Reduce on historical booking/search logs. One partition contains 70% of the data while the others are tiny. Explain why adding more processors may fail to improve completion time and connect the answer to the pattern's constraints and overhead.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Map-Reduce benefits depend on dividing the data into similar-sized subsets. A dominant partition becomes a straggler/bottleneck, leaving other processors idle and eroding parallel speedup. Infrastructure still incurs deployment/shuffle/sort/monitoring overhead. Stateless maps/key-value communication do not solve skew automatically; data partitioning must support balanced work. Applied to the **Flight Booking System**, this means the named Flight Booking System elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q03717 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Distinction  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q4  
**Scenario:** Flight Booking System  

A diagram for the Flight Booking System labels 'Presentation', 'Business' and 'Data'. A student concludes it is definitely a Layer pattern. Explain why the labels alone are insufficient and show how the **same names** could describe either Layer or Multi-Tier depending on element/relation semantics.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Layer is a **module pattern**: implementation units grouped into layers with allowed-to-use dependency rules. Multi-Tier is an **allocation/runtime pattern**: runtime components grouped into tiers with communication/allocation constraints. Box labels do not determine semantics. Ask whether the elements are modules and dependencies, or runtime components/tier groupings mapped to platforms. Applied to the **Flight Booking System**, this means the named Flight Booking System elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q03718 — Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Bridging and upward calls  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** E-Commerce Marketplace  

In the E-Commerce Marketplace, a strict Layer design is A→B→C. The team proposes (i) A directly uses C for performance and (ii) C emits a one-way callback/event upward to A without depending on a returned answer. Analyze both proposals using the lecture's finer points.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

A→C is **bridging**: it may be permitted, but must be explicitly documented; it can reduce traversal overhead while weakening dependency restriction/modifiability. An **upward call** is not automatically an upward *use*: the lecture defines 'uses' in terms of depending on the answer. A one-way upward notification can be allowed if it does not create a dependency on a response. Be explicit about the relation semantics. Applied to the **E-Commerce Marketplace**, this means the named E-Commerce Marketplace elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

</details>

## Q03719 — Publish-Subscribe (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Variant selection  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** E-Commerce Marketplace  

The E-Commerce Marketplace must distribute events related to 'a saved product goes on sale'. Compare **list-based, broadcast-based and content-based** Publish-Subscribe. Choose a variant for a case with many subscribers but highly selective event predicates and justify the trade-off.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose content-based Publish-Subscribe for the E-Commerce Marketplace.** List-based delivery is runtime-efficient but maintains explicit subscription lists; broadcast-based is simple and decoupled but makes every subscriber inspect irrelevant events. Content-based matching evaluates event attributes against subscriber predicates, so it fits many subscribers with highly selective interests. The trade-off is extra matching/indexing complexity and latency, which should be measured against the event-delivery response target.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_10_CCPatterns_Publish-Subscribe.pdf

</details>

## Q03720 — Peer-to-Peer (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Discovery, hops and supernodes  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** E-Commerce Marketplace  

In a P2P feature for the E-Commerce Marketplace, peers cannot broadcast discovery indefinitely. Explain the role of search propagation, **hop limits**, and **supernodes**, and show one quality trade-off caused by tightening the hop limit.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Search may propagate peer-to-peer for a bounded number of hops; hop limits control network overhead. Specialized peers/supernodes may index or route searches so ordinary peers reach more resources efficiently. A tighter hop limit can improve performance/network overhead/predictability but reduce discoverability/availability of rare resources. A supernode can improve discovery but may concentrate responsibility and require availability/security hardening. Applied to the **E-Commerce Marketplace**, this means the named E-Commerce Marketplace elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

Applied to the **Food Delivery Platform**, this means the named Food Delivery Platform elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q03742 — Model-View-Controller (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Many views and constraints  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Food Delivery Platform  

The Food Delivery Platform displays the same model through a table, chart and mobile visualization. Explain how MVC keeps them synchronized, why many views/controllers can share one model, and why the lecture constraint that the model should not directly interact with the controller matters.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Model holds application data/state and notifies views of changes; views render/query model; controllers translate user gestures into model/view actions. Multiple views/controllers can share one model because presentation/input concerns are separated. Preventing direct model→controller dependency helps preserve separation and reduces coupling; notifications from model go to interested views rather than making model dependent on specific input-control logic. Applied to the **Food Delivery Platform**, this means the named Food Delivery Platform elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_5_CCPatterns_Model-view Controller.pdf

</details>

## Q03743 — Map-Reduce (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Partition imbalance  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Food Delivery Platform  

The Food Delivery Platform uses Map-Reduce on city-wide delivery history. One partition contains 70% of the data while the others are tiny. Explain why adding more processors may fail to improve completion time and connect the answer to the pattern's constraints and overhead.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Map-Reduce benefits depend on dividing the data into similar-sized subsets. A dominant partition becomes a straggler/bottleneck, leaving other processors idle and eroding parallel speedup. Infrastructure still incurs deployment/shuffle/sort/monitoring overhead. Stateless maps/key-value communication do not solve skew automatically; data partitioning must support balanced work. Applied to the **Food Delivery Platform**, this means the named Food Delivery Platform elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q03744 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Distinction  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q4  
**Scenario:** Food Delivery Platform  

A diagram for the Food Delivery Platform labels 'Presentation', 'Business' and 'Data'. A student concludes it is definitely a Layer pattern. Explain why the labels alone are insufficient and show how the **same names** could describe either Layer or Multi-Tier depending on element/relation semantics.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Layer is a **module pattern**: implementation units grouped into layers with allowed-to-use dependency rules. Multi-Tier is an **allocation/runtime pattern**: runtime components grouped into tiers with communication/allocation constraints. Box labels do not determine semantics. Ask whether the elements are modules and dependencies, or runtime components/tier groupings mapped to platforms. Applied to the **Food Delivery Platform**, this means the named Food Delivery Platform elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q03745 — Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Bridging and upward calls  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Hospital Information System  

In the Hospital Information System, a strict Layer design is A→B→C. The team proposes (i) A directly uses C for performance and (ii) C emits a one-way callback/event upward to A without depending on a returned answer. Analyze both proposals using the lecture's finer points.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

A→C is **bridging**: it may be permitted, but must be explicitly documented; it can reduce traversal overhead while weakening dependency restriction/modifiability. An **upward call** is not automatically an upward *use*: the lecture defines 'uses' in terms of depending on the answer. A one-way upward notification can be allowed if it does not create a dependency on a response. Be explicit about the relation semantics. Applied to the **Hospital Information System**, this means the named Hospital Information System elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

</details>

## Q03746 — Publish-Subscribe (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Variant selection  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Hospital Information System  

The Hospital Information System must distribute events related to 'a critical lab value is recorded'. Compare **list-based, broadcast-based and content-based** Publish-Subscribe. Choose a variant for a case with many subscribers but highly selective event predicates and justify the trade-off.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose content-based Publish-Subscribe for the Hospital Information System.** List-based delivery is runtime-efficient but maintains explicit subscription lists; broadcast-based is simple and decoupled but makes every subscriber inspect irrelevant events. Content-based matching evaluates event attributes against subscriber predicates, so it fits many subscribers with highly selective interests. The trade-off is extra matching/indexing complexity and latency, which should be measured against the event-delivery response target.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_10_CCPatterns_Publish-Subscribe.pdf

</details>

## Q03747 — Peer-to-Peer (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Discovery, hops and supernodes  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Hospital Information System  

In a P2P feature for the Hospital Information System, peers cannot broadcast discovery indefinitely. Explain the role of search propagation, **hop limits**, and **supernodes**, and show one quality trade-off caused by tightening the hop limit.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Search may propagate peer-to-peer for a bounded number of hops; hop limits control network overhead. Specialized peers/supernodes may index or route searches so ordinary peers reach more resources efficiently. A tighter hop limit can improve performance/network overhead/predictability but reduce discoverability/availability of rare resources. A supernode can improve discovery but may concentrate responsibility and require availability/security hardening. Applied to the **Hospital Information System**, this means the named Hospital Information System elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q03748 — Pipe-and-Filter (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Pipeline parallelism  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Hospital Information System  

Three items T1, T2 and T3 are processed in the Hospital Information System by Filter A→Filter B→Filter C. Give a valid simultaneous execution snapshot, explain how buffering enables it, then identify why this improves **throughput** without necessarily reducing the end-to-end **latency** of one item.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Example snapshot: A processes T3, B processes T2, C processes T1. Pipes/buffers decouple stage timing until buffers fill, allowing concurrent stage execution. This can increase aggregate throughput because several items are in flight, but T1 still must traverse all mandatory stages, so its own end-to-end latency may remain the sum of stage/queue delays. Applied to the **Hospital Information System**, this means the named Hospital Information System elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

</details>

## Q03749 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Brutal, 7 marks)

**Type:** ESB, registry, orchestration  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Hospital Information System  

The Hospital Information System uses SOA. Distinguish the roles of a **service registry**, **ESB**, and **orchestration server**. For each, give one benefit and one new risk/overhead. Explain why none of the three is automatically required in every SOA instance.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Registry: providers register and consumers discover services, hiding provider location/identity and improving modifiability; adds discovery dependency/complexity. ESB: routes/transforms protocols/content and can perform security checks, improving interoperability/modifiability; adds latency and failure point. Orchestration server: coordinates multi-service business workflows; adds centralized coordination complexity/failure risk. They are optional architectural elements chosen according to the specific SOA problem. Applied to the **Hospital Information System**, this means the named Hospital Information System elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

Explain why the labels alone are insufficient and show how the **same names** could describe either Layer or Multi-Tier depending on element/relation semantics.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Layer is a **module pattern**: implementation units grouped into layers with allowed-to-use dependency rules. Multi-Tier is an **allocation/runtime pattern**: runtime components grouped into tiers with communication/allocation constraints. Box labels do not determine semantics. Ask whether the elements are modules and dependencies, or runtime components/tier groupings mapped to platforms. Applied to the **Ride-Hailing Platform**, this means the named Ride-Hailing Platform elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q03772 — Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Bridging and upward calls  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Video Streaming Service  

In the Video Streaming Service, a strict Layer design is A→B→C. The team proposes (i) A directly uses C for performance and (ii) C emits a one-way callback/event upward to A without depending on a returned answer. Analyze both proposals using the lecture's finer points.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

A→C is **bridging**: it may be permitted, but must be explicitly documented; it can reduce traversal overhead while weakening dependency restriction/modifiability. An **upward call** is not automatically an upward *use*: the lecture defines 'uses' in terms of depending on the answer. A one-way upward notification can be allowed if it does not create a dependency on a response. Be explicit about the relation semantics. Applied to the **Video Streaming Service**, this means the named Video Streaming Service elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

</details>

## Q03773 — Publish-Subscribe (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Variant selection  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Video Streaming Service  

The Video Streaming Service must distribute events related to 'a followed series releases an episode'. Compare **list-based, broadcast-based and content-based** Publish-Subscribe. Choose a variant for a case with many subscribers but highly selective event predicates and justify the trade-off.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose content-based Publish-Subscribe for the Video Streaming Service.** List-based delivery is runtime-efficient but maintains explicit subscription lists; broadcast-based is simple and decoupled but makes every subscriber inspect irrelevant events. Content-based matching evaluates event attributes against subscriber predicates, so it fits many subscribers with highly selective interests. The trade-off is extra matching/indexing complexity and latency, which should be measured against the event-delivery response target.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_10_CCPatterns_Publish-Subscribe.pdf

</details>

## Q03774 — Peer-to-Peer (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Discovery, hops and supernodes  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Video Streaming Service  

In a P2P feature for the Video Streaming Service, peers cannot broadcast discovery indefinitely. Explain the role of search propagation, **hop limits**, and **supernodes**, and show one quality trade-off caused by tightening the hop limit.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Search may propagate peer-to-peer for a bounded number of hops; hop limits control network overhead. Specialized peers/supernodes may index or route searches so ordinary peers reach more resources efficiently. A tighter hop limit can improve performance/network overhead/predictability but reduce discoverability/availability of rare resources. A supernode can improve discovery but may concentrate responsibility and require availability/security hardening. Applied to the **Video Streaming Service**, this means the named Video Streaming Service elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q03775 — Pipe-and-Filter (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Pipeline parallelism  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Video Streaming Service  

Three items T1, T2 and T3 are processed in the Video Streaming Service by Filter A→Filter B→Filter C. Give a valid simultaneous execution snapshot, explain how buffering enables it, then identify why this improves **throughput** without necessarily reducing the end-to-end **latency** of one item.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Example snapshot: A processes T3, B processes T2, C processes T1. Pipes/buffers decouple stage timing until buffers fill, allowing concurrent stage execution. This can increase aggregate throughput because several items are in flight, but T1 still must traverse all mandatory stages, so its own end-to-end latency may remain the sum of stage/queue delays. Applied to the **Video Streaming Service**, this means the named Video Streaming Service elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

</details>

## Q03776 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Brutal, 7 marks)

**Type:** ESB, registry, orchestration  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Video Streaming Service  

The Video Streaming Service uses SOA. Distinguish the roles of a **service registry**, **ESB**, and **orchestration server**. For each, give one benefit and one new risk/overhead. Explain why none of the three is automatically required in every SOA instance.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Registry: providers register and consumers discover services, hiding provider location/identity and improving modifiability; adds discovery dependency/complexity. ESB: routes/transforms protocols/content and can perform security checks, improving interoperability/modifiability; adds latency and failure point. Orchestration server: coordinates multi-service business workflows; adds centralized coordination complexity/failure risk. They are optional architectural elements chosen according to the specific SOA problem. Applied to the **Video Streaming Service**, this means the named Video Streaming Service elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q03777 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Replication and coupling  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Video Streaming Service  

The Video Streaming Service uses Shared-Data. The architect replicates the data store across two regions to reduce outage risk. Explain what quality may improve, then identify two new issues introduced by replication and one coupling problem that remains even if producers/consumers do not know each other.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Replication can improve availability and possibly read performance. New issues include consistency/synchronization, conflict resolution, replication latency, failover routing and operational complexity. Producer/consumer identity coupling is reduced, but accessors can still be coupled through knowledge of the shared **data schema/structure**. Applied to the **Video Streaming Service**, this means the named Video Streaming Service elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q03778 — Model-View-Controller (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Many views and constraints  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Video Streaming Service  

The Video Streaming Service displays the same model through a table, chart and mobile visualization. Explain how MVC keeps them synchronized, why many views/controllers can share one model, and why the lecture constraint that the model should not directly interact with the controller matters.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Model holds application data/state and notifies views of changes; views render/query model; controllers translate user gestures into model/view actions. Multiple views/controllers can share one model because presentation/input concerns are separated. Preventing direct model→controller dependency helps preserve separation and reduces coupling; notifications from model go to interested views rather than making model dependent on specific input-control logic. Applied to the **Video Streaming Service**, this means the named Video Streaming Service elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_5_CCPatterns_Model-view Controller.pdf

</details>

## Q03779 — Map-Reduce (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Partition imbalance  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Video Streaming Service  

The Video Streaming Service uses Map-Reduce on viewing telemetry. One partition contains 70% of the data while the others are tiny. Explain why adding more processors may fail to improve completion time and connect the answer to the pattern's constraints and overhead.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Map-Reduce benefits depend on dividing the data into similar-sized subsets. A dominant partition becomes a straggler/bottleneck, leaving other processors idle and eroding parallel speedup. Infrastructure still incurs deployment/shuffle/sort/monitoring overhead. Stateless maps/key-value communication do not solve skew automatically; data partitioning must support balanced work. Applied to the **Video Streaming Service**, this means the named Video Streaming Service elements must exhibit those exact relations; the labels alone are insufficient.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q03781 — Other Allocation Patterns (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Work assignment patterns  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

The University Student Portal will be developed by teams across three countries. Compare the **Platform**, **Competence Center**, and **Open Source** work-assignment patterns and choose one for a situation where one site has unique security expertise.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

**Choose Competence Center for the University Student Portal.** Assign the security-sensitive modules, threat analysis and security reviews to the site with unique expertise, while other sites consume its documented interfaces and guidance. A Platform arrangement instead gives one site ownership of reusable core assets, which fits product-family reuse rather than scarce expertise. Open Source distributes work among largely independent contributors and offers autonomy, but weaker centralized assignment/control makes it unsuitable for the stated specialist-security responsibility. The Competence Center gains expert consistency but risks a bottleneck and cross-site coordination dependency, so backup ownership and review schedules are required.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_14_AllocationPatterns_Other Allocation Patterns.pdf

</details>
